summary: The exact candidate correctly implements the SGLang side of a capability-gated LMCache MP cache_salt handoff and safely disables external caching for salted requests on legacy connectors. It is an acceptable partial fix and fail-closed mitigation, not a complete original-issue resolution: current/released LMCache lacks the required capability and token-plus-salt wire-key API.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X was visible with ROCm 7.2 and Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but LMCache was absent. An unrelated GPU smoke would not validate external cache-key tenant isolation.
remaining_counterexamples: With current LMCache dev or an existing released connector, supports_cache_salt is absent, so every salted request bypasses LMCache rather than producing token-plus-salt external keys.
No live LMCache daemon/object-key trace confirms that two identical prompts with different salts create distinct external keys; the prepared environment lacks LMCache.
The original end-to-end cross-tenant latency/compute scenario remains unverified here because the required LMCache package, daemon, and deployment setup are unavailable.
The coordinated LMCache PR 4842 is still open with mergeStateStatus DIRTY, so the required external API is not yet an available dependency.
remaining_limitations: This validates MP-mode SGLang handoff and fail-closed behavior only; it is not a full model-serving or live external-storage reproduction.
LMCache IP/XPU mode and extra_key/LoRA external namespacing are outside the candidate and original cache_salt MP scope.
No native code changed; native rebuild and ISA validation were not applicable.
The candidate PR prose reports four failing-before tests, while the exact committed five-test file produced five failures on the recorded base.
